concept.name: OpenTelemetry Tail-Based Trace Sampling & Span Context Propagation

relationships.description: Consistent hashing on trace_id routes all spans of a distributed trace to the same collector.

concept.tagline: Keep 100% of production errors and p99 latency spikes while cutting trace storage costs by 95% using two-tier OpenTelemetry tail sampling.
concept.purpose: Master W3C traceparent propagation, trace_id consistent-hash routing, 30s tail-buffer sizing, memory_limiter guards, and ring draining.

spark.summary: Tail-based sampling routes all spans of a trace by trace_id to one stateful collector, waits 30s, and keeps 100% of errors and slow traces while dropping 95%+ of healthy noise.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, pair stateless Tier 1 trace_id consistent-hash routers with memory-bounded Tier 2 tail-sampling collectors and 30s preStop draining.
spark.byteSummary:
At 1,000,000 spans/second, storing 100% of distributed traces in ClickHouse or Grafana Tempo costs tens of thousands of dollars per day for mostly healthy 200 OK traffic. **Head-Based Sampling** (deciding `keep` or `drop` at the ingress API gateway with a 1% coin flip) cuts storage by 99%, but it makes that decision **before** downstream microservices execute—meaning 99% of rare HTTP 500s, deadlocks, and p99 latency spikes are thrown away blindly.

**Tail-Based Sampling** flips the decision to the end of the trace's lifecycle. Microservices propagate a W3C `traceparent` header across HTTP/gRPC/Kafka boundaries and export 100% of spans to a **Two-Tier OpenTelemetry Collector** architecture: Tier 1 (`loadbalancingexporter`) hashes every span's `trace_id` consistently so all spans of the same trace land on the exact same Tier 2 stateful collector. Tier 2 buffers the trace in RAM for a `decision_wait` window (e.g., 30 seconds) and then evaluates sampling policies over the **complete** trace—retaining 100% of errors, 100% of slow traces (`duration > 500 ms`), VIP debug tenants, and a 1% baseline of healthy traffic.

The primary trade-off is stateful collector memory: buffering 30 seconds of spans requires strict `memory_limiter` circuit breakers, graceful consistent-hash ring draining during autoscaling, and async Kafka buffering before ClickHouse writes.

learningJourney.title: Why 1% Head-Based Sampling Misses 99% of Production Errors
learningJourney.purpose: Contrast blind ingress head-sampling against complete-trace tail-based policy evaluation.

explanation.foundation: Head-based sampling flips a coin at the API gateway (`sampled = hash(trace_id) % 100 == 0`). Because downstream DB timeouts and 500 errors haven't happened yet, 99% of incident traces are dropped before they even begin.
explanation.core: Tail-based sampling buffers all spans of a trace for a 30-second `decision_wait` window and decides keep/drop only after the root and child spans have arrived—capturing 100% of errors and slow outliers while still dropping 95%+ of healthy noise.
explanation.deepDive: You can still combine both: use cheap head-based rate limiting on known ultra-noisy health-check routes (`/healthz`) while sending business APIs through tail sampling.

learningJourney.title: W3C traceparent Propagation & Trace-ID Consistent-Hash Routing
learningJourney.purpose: Keep distributed spans linked across HTTP/gRPC/Kafka and route them to the same stateful collector by trace_id.

explanation.foundation: Every service injects the W3C `traceparent: 00-<trace_id>-<parent_span_id>-01` header into outbound HTTP, gRPC, and Kafka headers.
explanation.core: Because a single trace spans 10+ microservices, round-robin load balancing would scatter its spans across 10 different collectors—breaking tail evaluation. Tier 1 collectors use `loadbalancingexporter` with consistent hashing on `trace_id`.
explanation.deepDive: When a trace arrives at Tier 2, all spans with the same 128-bit `trace_id` converge in one collector's in-memory `trace_id -> SpanList` map.

sectionDiagram.title: W3C traceparent Propagation & Trace-ID Consistent-Hash Routing

cards.label: Async Queue Propagation
cards.detail: Inject traceparent into Kafka/SQS message headers so background consumer spans stay linked.

cards.label: Why Round-Robin Breaks Tail
cards.detail: If Span 1 lands on Collector A and Error Span 5 lands on Collector B, A drops the trace as healthy!

cards.label: Two-Tier Separation
cards.detail: Tier 1 is stateless and cheap to scale; Tier 2 holds the 30s stateful trace buffer.

sectionDiagram.summary: Consistent hashing on W3C trace_id at Tier 1 guarantees every span of a distributed trace converges on one Tier 2 collector.
sectionDiagram.caption: Consistent hashing on W3C trace_id at Tier 1 guarantees every span of a distributed trace converges on one Tier 2 collector.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement OpenTelemetry Tail-Based Trace Sampling & Span Context Propagation without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, pair stateless Tier 1 trace_id consistent-hash routers with memory-bounded Tier 2 tail-sampling collectors and 30s preStop draining.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When OpenTelemetry Tail-Based Trace Sampling & Span Context Propagation experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Bounded Trace-Buffer Evaluator with Policy Rules & Memory Guard
learningJourney.purpose: Implement a deterministic tail-sampling evaluator that prioritizes errors, latency outliers, and bounded memory.

explanation.foundation: A tail-sampling evaluator must check error status, total trace duration, debug flags, and deterministic baseline hashing.
explanation.deepDive: Using `sha256(trace_id) % 100` for the 1% baseline makes sampling deterministic across restarts without mutable RNG state.

sectionDiagram.title: Bounded Trace-Buffer Evaluator with Policy Rules & Memory Guard

cards.label: True End-to-End Duration
cards.detail: Computing max_end - min_start across all spans catches slow traces even if the root span timed out.

cards.label: Deterministic Baseline
cards.detail: Hashing trace_id modulo 100 gives repeatable baseline sampling rates.

cards.label: Strict Bounds
cards.detail: Validating sample_pct in [0, 100] prevents silent config typos from dropping 100% of traces.

sectionDiagram.summary: Scanning spans for errors, computing full trace duration, and hashing trace_id for baseline sampling keep high-signal traces.
sectionDiagram.caption: Scanning spans for errors, computing full trace duration, and hashing trace_id for baseline sampling keep high-signal traces.

learningJourney.title: Sizing 30-Second Trace Buffers & Bounding Collector RAM
learningJourney.purpose: Calculate exact collector RAM for 1M spans/sec over a 30s decision_wait and tune num_traces caps.

explanation.foundation: Buffering 1,000,000 spans/sec for 30 seconds holds 30,000,000 active spans in RAM simultaneously.
explanation.core: At ~1.5 KB per serialized OTLP span, 30M spans require ~45 GB of collector RAM across the Tier 2 pool (e.g., 16 collector pods x 4 GB heap each, leaving ~30% headroom).
explanation.deepDive: Set `num_traces` and `expected_new_traces_per_sec` in OTel `tail_sampling` processor to pre-size hash maps and evict oldest traces gracefully if a traffic spike exceeds RAM.

sectionDiagram.title: Sizing 30-Second Trace Buffers & Bounding Collector RAM

cards.label: Decision-Wait Trade-Off
cards.detail: Longer decision_wait (30s) captures slow async jobs; shorter wait (10s) cuts collector RAM by 3x.

cards.label: Attribute Stripping
cards.detail: Strip bulky SQL/HTTP body attributes at Tier 1 before buffering in Tier 2 to halve span size.

cards.label: Headroom Margin
cards.detail: Always size Tier 2 RAM with 30-40% headroom for GC pauses and 2x traffic bursts.

sectionDiagram.summary: Sizing Tier 2 collectors for 30s x spans/sec with Tier 1 attribute stripping and num_traces caps prevents OOMKills.
sectionDiagram.caption: Sizing Tier 2 collectors for 30s x spans/sec with Tier 1 attribute stripping and num_traces caps prevents OOMKills.

learningJourney.title: Memory_Limiter Backpressure & Noisy-Tenant Span Shedding
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent a single runaway debug service from OOMing Tier 2 collectors using memory_limiter and per-tenant caps.

explanation.foundation: If a misconfigured service enters an infinite retry loop and emits 500K spans/sec for one trace, it can OOMKill Tier 2 Collector #7.
explanation.core: Place OTel's `memory_limiter` processor first in every pipeline (`limit_percentage: 80`, `spike_limit_percentage: 25`) to refuse new spans and force `runtime.GC()` before hitting cgroup limits.
explanation.deepDive: Cap `max_spans_per_trace` (e.g., 10,000 spans) so runaway loop traces are truncated/evaluated early instead of pinning RAM.

sectionDiagram.title: Memory_Limiter Backpressure & Noisy-Tenant Span Shedding

cards.label: Observability Never Crashes Apps
cards.detail: OTel SDKs use non-blocking ring buffers; collector backpressure drops telemetry, never user requests.

cards.label: Span-Count Cap
cards.detail: Capping spans per trace stops giant batch-job traces from starving normal API traces.

cards.label: Per-Tenant Rate Limit
cards.detail: Apply token-bucket span quotas per tenant_id at Tier 1.

sectionDiagram.summary: 80% memory_limiter breakers, 10K-span trace caps, and non-blocking SDKs isolate telemetry spikes from app traffic.
sectionDiagram.caption: 80% memory_limiter breakers, 10K-span trace caps, and non-blocking SDKs isolate telemetry spikes from app traffic.

learningJourney.title: Graceful Consistent-Hash Ring Draining & Kafka Export Buffering
learningJourney.purpose: Avoid splitting in-flight traces during Tier 2 deploys and absorb ClickHouse write spikes via Kafka.

explanation.foundation: Autoscaling Tier 2 collectors changes the consistent-hash ring, causing spans arriving at t=15s to route to a different pod than t=0s.
explanation.core: During rolling deploys, use two-phase draining: remove the terminating pod from Tier 1 DNS/endpoints first, wait `decision_wait` (30s) to flush its buffered traces, then exit.
explanation.deepDive: Write sampled traces to a **Kafka** topic before ingesting into **ClickHouse** so backend DB maintenance never causes Tier 2 OOMs.

sectionDiagram.title: Graceful Consistent-Hash Ring Draining & Kafka Export Buffering

cards.label: 30s PreStop Hook
cards.detail: A Kubernetes preStop sleep >= decision_wait lets draining collectors evaluate and flush all buffered traces.

cards.label: Kafka Shock Absorber
cards.detail: Decoupling collectors from ClickHouse prevents DB compaction pauses from backing up collector RAM.

cards.label: Static Sizing Over Rapid Churn
cards.detail: Use slower HPA cooldowns (5-10 min) on Tier 2 to minimize hash-ring remapping.

sectionDiagram.summary: 30s preStop ring draining and Kafka export buffering prevent split traces and storage-induced collector OOMs.
sectionDiagram.caption: 30s preStop ring draining and Kafka export buffering prevent split traces and storage-induced collector OOMs.

learningJourney.title: Monitoring Collector Drop Rates, Decision Latency & Incomplete Traces
learningJourney.purpose: Meta-monitor the tracing pipeline itself for memory-limiter drops, orphan spans, and ClickHouse lag.

explanation.foundation: If the tracing pipeline silently drops spans, engineers lose visibility right when an outage occurs.
explanation.deepDive: Alert immediately if `refused_spans > 0` or if `incomplete_rootless_trace_ratio > 5%` (indicating Tier 1 hash-ring drift).

sectionDiagram.title: Monitoring Collector Drop Rates, Decision Latency & Incomplete Traces

cards.label: Synthetic Error Canary
cards.detail: Emit a tagged error trace every 60s and assert it lands in ClickHouse within 45s.

cards.label: Rootless-Trace Alert
cards.detail: Rising traces missing their root span point to mismatched Tier 1 hash rings or <30s decision_wait.

cards.label: FinOps Guardrail
cards.detail: Track daily ingested GB/day per service to catch accidental debug-flag leaks.

sectionDiagram.summary: Synthetic error canaries, refused-span alerts, and rootless-trace ratios keep the tracing pipeline trustworthy.
sectionDiagram.caption: Synthetic error canaries, refused-span alerts, and rootless-trace ratios keep the tracing pipeline trustworthy.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does 1% head-based sampling at the API gateway fail during a microservice incident?

options.text: The gateway makes the keep/drop decision before downstream services execute, blindly dropping 99% of traces that later fail with 500s or high latency.
options.feedback: Correct! At t=0 ms, the gateway has no knowledge of downstream failures.

options.text: Head-based sampling corrupts the W3C traceparent header.
options.feedback: traceparent is propagated normally; the issue is premature dropping at ingress.
ClickHouse stores any spans exported to it.

options.text: Head-based sampling buffers spans in RAM for 30 seconds.
options.feedback: Buffering for decision_wait is tail-based sampling, not head-based.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Head-based sampling decides before downstream errors or tail latency occur, discarding 99% of incident traces.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if Tier 1 OpenTelemetry collectors forward spans to Tier 2 tail-sampling collectors using round-robin load balancing instead of consistent hashing on `trace_id`?

options.text: Spans from the same trace scatter across different Tier 2 collectors, breaking error/latency evaluation and producing incomplete traces.
options.feedback: Correct! All spans sharing a trace_id must land on the exact same Tier 2 collector.

options.text: Tier 2 collectors automatically replicate every span to all peers.
options.feedback: Standard OTel tail-sampling collectors do not broadcast spans across peers.

options.text: gRPC automatically merges spans from different pods.
options.feedback: gRPC load balancing has no awareness of trace_id grouping without explicit routing.

options.text: It reduces collector RAM usage by 50%.
options.feedback: Total span volume is identical, but trace assembly breaks.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Consistent hashing on trace_id is mandatory so all spans of a trace converge on one stateful collector.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a Tier 2 tail-sampling collector pod wait `decision_wait` (e.g., 30 seconds) after being removed from Tier 1 routing before shutting down?

options.text: To finish buffering, evaluating, and flushing all in-flight traces already held in its 30-second RAM window without splitting or dropping them.
options.feedback: Correct! A preStop drain >= decision_wait prevents abrupt loss of in-flight traces during rolling deploys.

options.text: To allow ClickHouse to re-index its primary key.
options.feedback: ClickHouse indexing is independent of collector shutdown.

options.text: To wait for W3C traceparent headers to expire.
options.feedback: traceparent headers do not have a 30s expiration.

options.text: To let the Linux kernel flush UDP GSO packets.
options.feedback: OTLP exports over gRPC/HTTP TCP, and the 30s wait matches decision_wait.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Waiting decision_wait after leaving the Tier 1 hash ring lets buffered traces complete evaluation cleanly.

prerequisites.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
